items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: I never did do any talking to Freddie at all.

ctx.x: Did you ever talk to Freddie Kepa about that?

I never did do any talking to Freddie at all. I can remember just how high Freddie, or one of them things. Freddie didn't want to record because he said he'd steal his stuff. See he didn't want to record. Last I saw Freddie became sick. Freddie was a big man around 250. And he came down the last time I saw him, it looked like he was about 160 or something like that. I do believe, well I don't know, it could have been most anything was wrong, but he died, he should have died. He'd come into the club room and get…
You never heard him play? No, as I know of.

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: We met Joe Oliver, Freddie Kebitt, Manny Poiré, so I knew those fellas in New Orleans before I left.

ctx.x: So when was the first music that you were interested in? Did you start on the trombone or which instrument did you start on?

Well, my first instrument was trombone, but it wasn't my favorite instrument. I'd like to tell you, Bill, about how I come to study the trombone. While talking with Joe Oliver, it must have been somewhere around 1920, 1921, somewhere along there. He, I told Joe Oliver that I was going to take lessons on the trombone. So he says, why don't you try the clarinet? The reason Joe suggested to me to take the, take up the clarinet was because I used to whistle so good. And he said people did. So he thought if a fella…
